statements.quote: We anticipate our full year 2025 capital expenditures will be in the range of $60-65 billion.
statements.notes: Total capex guidance; this sentence itself does not mention AI. The link to generative AI is in the next sentence of the same passage. Not an AI amount.

statements.quote: We expect capex growth in 2025 will be driven by increased investment to support both our generative AI efforts and our core business.
These are all big investments -- especially the hundreds of billions of dollars that we will invest in AI infrastructure over the long term.
statements.notes: 'Hundreds of billions' over 'the long term' is not a stated range or a single fiscal year, so it is recorded as qualitative. A null year should not be defaulted to 2025, because this is a multi-year statement. The field is assumed to be capex (AI infrastructure).

statements.quote: On the data center side, we’re anticipating higher data center spend in 2025 to be driven by build-outs of our large training clusters and our higher power density data centers that are entering the core construction phase.
statements.notes: The AI link is through 'large training clusters'. The sentence does not say 'AI' explicitly.

statements.quote: And then in terms of the breakdown for core versus Gen AI use cases, we’re expecting total infrastructure spend within each of Gen AI, non-AI and core AI to increase in ‘25 with the majority of our CapEx directed to our core business with some caveat that that is -- that’s not easy to measure perfectly as the data centers we’re building can support AI or non-AI workloads and the GPU- based servers we procure for gen AI can be repurposed for core AI use cases and so on and so forth.
statements.notes: The sentence says Gen AI and core AI infrastructure spend will increase in 2025, but gives no AI share. 'Majority to core business' is not an AI share, because core business includes core AI.

statements.quote: We are planning to significantly ramp up deployment of GPUs in 2025, and we’ll continue to engage with our vendors and invest in our own silicon to meet those needs.
statements.notes: GPU deployment is treated as AI capex. The sentence does not say 'AI' explicitly.

statements.quote: In 2025, we expect headcount growth will continue to be primarily driven by technical roles across our priority initiatives within infrastructure, monetization, Reality Labs, generative AI, as well as regulation and compliance.
statements.notes: Generative AI is one of several named drivers of headcount growth.

statements.quote: And here, growth in employee comp and headcount more broadly is primarily driven by those areas that I mentioned, infrastructure monetization, generative AI, Reality Labs, and regulation and compliance.
statements.notes: The preceding sentence refers to 2025 expense growth, but this sentence names no year. Generative AI is one of several drivers.

statements.quote: That’s what a lot of our new headcount growth is going towards.
statements.notes: 'That' refers to initiatives that use AI advances to grow revenue, described in a prior sentence. The AI link is indirect, and the sentence names no year (the context says 'next few years').
